clue.text: Vital force located out of action

put means placed or located

explanation.surface: A physicist notes that some vital energy has been stationed somewhere idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaput is slang for broken or no longer working, the state of a machine out of action.

clue.text: Contracting almost superfluous, supplying tools for craftspeople

parts.note: needless means superfluous

explanation.definitionFit: Knitting needles are the tools used by people who craft knitwear.

clue.text: Enlist crew before going on ship

indicators.note: going on means the ship abbreviation is added after

parts.note: pre means before
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Sailors are signed up before boarding a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To press men is to force them into naval service, as the press gang did with crews.

clue.text: Soldiers trapped by river in flood

indicators.note: trapped by means the soldiers go inside the river

parts.note: the Trent is a major English river
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are cut off by a river that has burst its banks.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent rush of water, a flood.

clue.text: Apply pressure to clothing being laundered

parts.note: a bra is an item of clothing
something in the wash is being laundered

explanation.surface: Instructions for squeezing garments while they go through the laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: To brainwash someone is to apply relentless psychological pressure until they change their beliefs.

clue.text: One that's stingy, following complaint

parts.note: a bee stings, so it is one that's stingy in a punning sense

explanation.surface: A miser comes in after a grievance is aired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stingy' looks like mean, but read it as able to sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is slang for a complaint or grievance.

clue.text: Prepared for instant action, they're a tad unsettled

indicators.note: unsettled means the letters of the phrase are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notes that people are a little nervous while poised to act.
explanation.definitionFit: At the ready means prepared and available for immediate use.

clue.text: To write up one chapter showing favouritism

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the words to and write are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: to pen is to write
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An author writes up a chapter that plays favourites.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotic describes nepotism, favouring relatives in appointments.

clue.text: Getting mean, elderly lady inside

indicators.note: inside means the lady goes within the elderly word

parts.note: aging means growing old, elderly
Vera is a lady's name

explanation.surface: An old woman indoors is becoming nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like nasty, but it is the arithmetic average.
explanation.definitionFit: Averaging means working out the mean of a set of numbers.

clue.text: England's the real source for this opera

indicators.note: source for says these words are the raw material, rearranged, for the answer

explanation.surface: A claim that England is the true origin of a certain opera.
explanation.walkthrough: The opera is by Humperdinck, a German, so the surface is cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Humperdinck's opera of 1893 is based on the fairy tale of the two lost children.

clue.text: I get closer to home — I'm not joking

parts.note: to near is to approach, or get closer
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone insists, quite seriously, that they are approaching their house.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue has a stray 'or' (OCR); the page prints 'I'm not joking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying you are in earnest is saying you are serious, which is what 'I'm not joking' conveys.

clue.text: Groom about to enter enclosure

indicators.note: to enter means one piece goes inside the enclosure word

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
re is Latin for about or concerning

explanation.surface: A stable groom is about to go into a paddock.
explanation.definitionFit: Groom as a verb means to tidy oneself, as a bird does when it preens its feathers.

clue.text: Part of maize plant rejected for fear that it contains arsenic

indicators.note: contains means the arsenic symbol goes inside the turned word
rejected means the words for fear that give a word that is turned back to front

parts.note: lest means for fear that
As is the chemical symbol for arsenic

explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' acts on LEST alone, before the arsenic goes in. The held clue's stray 'at' is OCR; the page has 'for fear that'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tassel is the male flower spike that sprouts at the top of a maize plant.

clue.text: Match-box — it sets a precedent

parts.note: a test is an international match, as in cricket
a case is a box

explanation.surface: A matchbox is described as a trendsetter.
explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a legal action whose ruling sets a precedent for later similar cases.

clue.text: Football club's vault mentioned in document

indicators.note: mentioned means the phrase is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: Man U is Manchester United football club, and a crypt is a vault

explanation.definitionFit: A manuscript is a handwritten or typed document.

clue.text: The margin's been altered — it's a dreadful experience

indicators.note: been altered says the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Someone finds having the page margins changed truly awful.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue's 'an' is OCR for 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a bad dream, and figuratively any terrifying or very unpleasant experience.

clue.text: Prepares to follow snooker player -and cracks up

definitions.meaning: goes to means prepares to, followed by pot, what a snooker player does

explanation.surface: Someone getting ready to copy a snooker star has a breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to pot is an idiom for deteriorating or going to ruin.

clue.text: Church in a foreign country

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church; the answer also runs forwards across 'Church in a', but the charade is the intended reading, so that is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A church situated somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: China is a country in East Asia, foreign to the British setter.

clue.text: What is required when daughter's born first, followed by son

indicators.note: first places the born word ahead of the daughter abbreviation
followed by puts the son abbreviation last

parts.note: née means born, used before a woman's maiden name
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A family's requirements when a daughter arrives before a son.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue's 'is' after daughter's is OCR; the page has 'daughter's born first'.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs are the things that are required or necessary.

clue.text: In other words, curtail the current run

parts.note: sc, for scilicet, means namely or in other words

indicators.note: curtail means the last letter is cut from the current word

parts.note: the ampere is the unit of electric current

explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run quickly and playfully.

clue.text: Exploding gun made a primarily deafening sound

primarily picks the first letter of deafening

explanation.surface: A gun goes off with a deafening bang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a noise, but it is the adjective meaning intact.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound as an adjective means in good condition, free of damage.

clue.text: Secretive person decapitated and buried in my tale of suspense

indicators.note: buried in means the beheaded piece goes inside the word my

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: decapitated means the first letter is removed

parts.note: an oyster is a secretive person, one who clams up

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped man is beheaded and buried, as told in a thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: A mystery is a detective story or thriller full of suspense.

clue.text: Transport's arrival

definitions.meaning: to transport is to carry away with delight, to enrapture
an arrival or coming in to a place

explanation.surface: Announcing that the transport has turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressed on the second syllable it means to enrapture; on the first it means an act of coming in.

clue.text: I climb, covering black line on map

indicators.note: covering means the climb word goes around the black abbreviation

parts.note: soar means climb high
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A climber covers a black line drawn on a map.

clue.text: Better opportunity to disclose damage

explanation.surface: An improved chance to reveal harm done.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers surpassing, revealing and damaging; the noun means a chance.

clue.text: Cutting a number of policemen

parts.note: the CID, Criminal Investigation Department, is a body of police detectives

explanation.surface: Reducing a number of police officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting remarks are sharp and sarcastic, which acid ones are too.

clue.text: Eagerly accept backing of an insect

indicators.note: backing means the word given by of an insect is read from the end

parts.note: pupal means relating to the pupa, a stage in an insect's life

explanation.surface: Someone happily takes the support offered by a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap up is to accept something eagerly, as a cat laps milk.

clue.text: Client upset about people being severe

indicators.note: about means the rearranged word goes around the people word
upset means the letters of client are knocked into a new order

parts.note: men means people

clue.text: Imbued unnamed planet with a man's name

parts.note: Saturn is a planet

clue.text: Peasant has a couple of animals left

parts.note: a yoke is a pair of oxen joined together

explanation.surface: A farmer has two beasts remaining.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is an unsophisticated country person, a rustic or peasant.
